flawed_step: Lines 0830–0832 incorrectly replace the exponential factor by exp((|x|-|x'|)^2/2) and then claim the resulting expression is O(1).
counterexample: Take x=2 and x'=-1. The expression on line 0830 equals (3/sqrt(2))exp(-1/2), whereas the purportedly equal expression on line 0831 equals (3/sqrt(2))exp(1/2). More generally, with x=t>0 and x'=-1, the line-0831 expression is ((t+1)/sqrt(t))exp((t-1)^2/2), which diverges as t→∞ and is not O(1).
assessment_summary: The proof relies on this false simplification to establish the uniform bound for the real-real kernel term. The correct exponent would have a minus sign; as written, the claimed equality and ensuing O(1) assertion are false.
